nodes.name: Co-Fe PBA hollow structures via self-templated growth
nodes.procedure: Three kinds of hollow Co-Fe PBA prepared by adjusting PVP and citrate concentration: cages, frames, boxes. Co-Fe PBA cubes form quickly as template. PVP/citrate stabilize (100)/(111) planes. New PBA deposits on reactive edges/corners. High citrate causes angular etching forming open cages.
nodes.source_text: Nai et al.[145] successfully prepared three kinds of hollow Co-Fe PBA with special morphology by adjusting concentration of PVP and citrate... framework showed best electrocatalytic performance

unit_operations.name: Cube templating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Co-Fe PBA cubes formed quickly serving as template

unit_operations.name: Frame formation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: presence of PVP makes Co-Fe PBA deposit forming surface-closed boxes

unit_operations.name: Cage etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: high concentration citrate results in angular etching forming open cage

nodes.name: H-KMF hollow PBA
nodes.procedure: Sodium citrate adsorbs Mn2+ through electrostatic interaction, competition with ferricyanide reduces KMF nanoparticle formation rate forming regular cubic structure. Remaining citrate adsorbs to KMF surface preventing further growth into cavity.
nodes.source_text: Jiang et al.[85] prepared hollow Mn-based Prussian blue analogues H-KMF with help of sodium citrate

nodes.name: MnCoPBA morphology evolution
nodes.procedure: SDS added, reaction kinetics dominated initially with (111) faces growing fast. SDS adsorbs on (111) inhibiting degradation and (100) growth. Thermodynamics causes (111) dissolution forming PBA-II, PBA-III core-shell, PBA-IV hollow cube.
nodes.source_text: Wang et al.[146] reported preparation of MnCoPBA with four different morphologies via adjusting reaction times by adding SDS

unit_operations.name: Core dissolution
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: PBA-IV hollow cube whose six faces etched

nodes.name: PB acid etching
nodes.procedure: Solid PB cube treated in 1.0 M HCl at 140°C for 4 h, cavity formed in solid structure.
nodes.source_text: Hu et al.[171] treated solid PB cube with uniform morphology... in 1.0 M HCl at 140°C for 4 h

nodes.name: NiFe PBA nanoframes
nodes.procedure: NiFe(II) PBA cubes etched in HCl: 5 min forms concave cubes, 1 h forms nanoframes. HCl destroys coordination bonds, middle part of outer surface dissolves quickly.
nodes.source_text: Zhang et al.[86] used organic-free preferential etching strategy... When treatment time reaches 1 h, special frame structure observed

unit_operations.name: Surface etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: after 5 min, smooth surface becomes concave

unit_operations.name: Frame formation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: treatment time reaches 1 h, frame structure observed

nodes.name: ZIF-67 to Co-Fe PBA
nodes.procedure: ZIF-67 hydrolyzes releasing Co ions, anion exchange with ferricyanide forms ZIF-67@Co-Fe PBA yolk-shell or hollow PBAs.
nodes.source_text: Wang et al.[151] synthesized ZIF-67/Co-Fe PBA yolk-shell nanoboxes using solid cubic ZIF-67 as precursor by anion exchange

nodes.name: NiCoP phosphidation
nodes.procedure: Ni-Co PBA nanoboxes prepared by ammonia etching, then high temperature heat treatment with NaH2PO2·H2O forms NiCoP-x-T hollow nanoboxes.
nodes.source_text: Wang et al.[118] designed NiCoP hollow nanobox... NiCoP-x-T obtained by series of high temperature heat treatment with NaH2PO2·H2O

unit_operations.name: Ammonia etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Ni-Co PBA nanoboxes prepared by etching with ammonia

unit_operations.name: Phosphating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: high temperature heat treatment with NaH2PO2

nodes.name: CoFe PBA phosphating
nodes.procedure: CoFe PBA hollow spheres with 100 nm shell thickness prepared by anion exchange with K3[Fe(CN)6] using Co-glycerate spheres, then phosphating forms Fe-Co_xP hollow spheres.
nodes.source_text: Song et al.[154] prepared CoFe PBA hollow spheres... Then Fe-Co_xP hollow spheres obtained by phosphating

unit_operations.name: Anion exchange
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: using Co-glycerase spheres as sacrificial templates at room temperature

nodes.name: CuCo-PBA calcination
nodes.procedure: CuCo-PBA nanocubes calcined forming hollow/porous CuO/Co3O4 heterostructures via Kirkendall effect. External surface adsorbs oxygen forming shell, metal ions diffuse outward faster than oxygen inward.
nodes.source_text: Tian et al.[119] synthesized CuO/Co3O4... using CuCoPBA as precursors elucidated formation mechanism based on Kirkendall effect

unit_operations.name: Thermal annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: external surface first adsorbs oxygen forming CuO/Co3O4 shell

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show NiFe(II) PBA evolution from cubes to concave cubes after 5 min HCl etching and to nanoframes after 1 h with consistent size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By observing the morphologies of NiFe(II) PBA in HCL at different times, after 5min, NiFe(II) PBA has no obvious size change, but the originally smooth surface of PBA becomes concave due to slight etching (Figure 6d,e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected-area electron diffraction (ED) patterns confirm similar single crystal structure for initial cubes and concave cubes, but different crystal structure for nanoframes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron diffraction (ED) results of the concave cubes and the initial cubes are similar, which indicates that they have similar single crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wide-angle XRD reveals initial NiFe(II) PBA has rhombohedral structure while final nanoframes have face-centered-cubic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD analysis shows that the initial NiFe(II) PBA is rhombohedral structure, and the final nanoframe is face-centered-cubic structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows surface evolution from smooth Co-glycerate spheres (10 min roughening) to nanoparticle-covered CoFe PBA after 6 h anion exchange.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM characterization results (Figure 9b) show the surface changes of the material during the anion exchange process. After 10min, the smooth surface of the original sphere began to become rough, and with the extension of the reaction time, more and more nanoparticles deposited on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms complete transformation from solid Co-glycerate structure to hollow CoFe PBA spheres during anion exchange process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM results (Figure 9c,e) reveal the transformation process from solid structure to hollow structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Fe doping reduces Co 2p peak position by 0.3 eV in Fe-Co_xP compared to Co_xP, indicating electronic coupling between Co and Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results of cobalt in Co_xP and Fe-Co_xP, it can be found that the doping of Fe element reduces the peak position of Co 2p by 0.3eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms CoMn-PBA HSs phase corresponds to standard card of K MnFe(CN)_6·nH_2O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing the XRD results (Figure 9k), it can be seen that the phase after the reaction corresponds to the standard card of K MnFe(CN)_6·nH_2O.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES confirms presence of Co element in final CoMn-PBA product.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) results show that the final product contains Co element.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms presence of Co element in final CoMn-PBA product.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) results show that the final product contains Co element.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM and TEM images show Co-Fe PBA boxes, cages, and frames morphologies controlled by PVP and citrate concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Field emission scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of Co-Fe PBA boxes cages and frames.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images document morphological evolution of MnCoPBA from solid PBA-I to hollow core-shell PBA-III to etched hollow cube PBA-IV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of MnCoPBA in different reaction stages can be observed by TEM (Figure 5f). PBA-I is a solid structure. PBA-II looks like a cross... PBA-IV is a hollow cube.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations show MnCoPBA surface energies: (111) -59.4 J cm^-2, (110) -14.2 J cm^-2, (100) -9.3 J cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 5g, the surface energy of (111), (110) and (100) in MnCoPBA were -59.4 J cm^-2, -14.2 J cm^-2 and -9.3 J cm^-2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows transformation from smooth solid Co-glycerate spheres to rough CoFe PBA nanoparticles after anion exchange.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM characterization results (Figure 9b) show the surface changes of the material during the anion exchange process. After 10min, the smooth surface of the original sphere began to become rough.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals CoFe PBA hollow spheres with shell thickness of about 100 nm formed from Co-glycerate templates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Song et al.[154] prepared CoFe PBA hollow spheres with a shell thickness of about 100nm by anion exchange reaction with K3[Fe(CN)6] using Co-glycerase spheres as sacrificial templates.
